title: AFL Player Salary: How to Convert Hourly Rates to Annual Pay with a 38-Hour Week
description: Convert any hourly rate to annual salary using a 38-hour week and 52-week year. Includes AFL player salary comparisons, minimum wage, casual loading, super, and tax estimates.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week, the national minimum wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week, and the calculator converts any hourly rate—even an AFL player salary—to annual, fortnightly, and after-tax figures.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your gross annual salary before tax and super. The calculator on this site does the maths for you, and also shows the fortnightly amount (weekly × 2).

faqs.q: What is the difference between the national minimum wage and award rates?
faqs.a: The national minimum wage is the minimum pay for employees not covered by an award or agreement. From 1 July 2026, that rate is $26.44 per hour or $1004.90 per week for 38 hours. Award rates are higher minimums set for specific industries and can include penalty rates and allowances. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for each award.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on top of my salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, if your annual salary is $80,000, your employer contributes an extra $9,600 into your super fund. The calculator on this site estimates super separately from your gross pay.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Hourly Rate and Annual Salary

Whether you're negotiating a new job, comparing offers, or simply curious about what your hourly rate means over a full year, converting hourly pay to an annual salary is straightforward. The standard formula used across Australia is:

**Hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks = gross annual salary**

For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week (the standard week under the National Employment Standards), the calculation becomes:

**Hourly rate × 38 × 52**

This gives you your annual pay before tax, super, and any deductions. The calculator on this site (the timesheet) does this instantly. You can also see your fortnightly pay by doubling the weekly amount.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The Fair Work Commission sets the national minimum wage each year. From 1 July 2026, the rate is **$26.44 per hour**, which equals **$1004.90 per week** for 38 hours. This is the minimum for adult employees not covered by an award or agreement.

Most employees, however, are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or role. For example, the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Industry Award (SCHADS) has specific pay rates that change from 1 December 2026. Always check the relevant award pay guide to ensure you're being paid correctly.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate because they don't get paid leave. For the national minimum wage, that means **$33.05 per hour** for casuals. The calculator includes a checkbox to add this loading automatically—never type a rate that already includes casual loading.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee is **12%** of your gross pay, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, on a $80,000 salary, your employer contributes an extra $9,600 into your super fund. The calculator shows this separately.

### Converting an AFL Player Salary

You might wonder how an AFL player salary compares to a typical hourly rate. While AFL players are usually paid annual contracts (often in the hundreds of thousands or millions), the same conversion formula works in reverse. If you know an AFL player's annual salary, you can divide by 52 and then by 38 to get an equivalent hourly rate. For instance, a $400,000 annual salary equals about $202 per hour. This site's calculator can help you make that conversion, though most AFL player salaries are far above the national average.

### Using the Calculator

The timesheet is the home page. Enter your base hourly rate (without casual loading). If you're casual, check the box to add 25% on top. The calculator then shows:

- Weekly pay (hourly × 38)
- Fortnightly pay (weekly × 2)
- Annual gross pay (weekly × 52)
- Estimated tax (using 2026–27 resident rates with the tax-free threshold)
- Medicare levy (2% of taxable income)
- Superannuation (12% on top, up to the cap)

For more details on minimum wages, see our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page. To understand casual loading better, visit [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading).

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

The tax estimate uses the 2026–27 resident tax brackets: nil on the first $18,200, then 15% up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is 2% of taxable income, with reductions for singles earning below a certain threshold. Note that HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not included. This is an estimate—always consult the Australian Taxation Office for your personal situation.

Remember, this calculator assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For award-specific rates, refer to the [pay guides](/blog) or [reference tables](/data).

Whether you're checking a standard job or curious about an AFL player salary, this tool gives you a clear picture of your annual, fortnightly, and take-home pay.
